newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans close higher on export inspections.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans close higher on export inspections.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures closed higher on bullish input from USDA's weekly export inspections report which showed the soybean number at a record level, traders said.
"They were record exports, the shipments were great," said Ron Kucha of Chicago trade house O'Connor and Co.

USDA Monday said 38.924 million bushels of U.S. soybeans were inspected for export at U.S. ports during the week ended November 14. That tally was well above trade expectations for 25 million to 30 million bushels.
USDA confirmed the inspections were a record.
USDA said the total broke the prior week's record of 33.4 million bushels plus the total for that week, ending November 7, was revised up sharply to 37 million bushels on Monday's report.
"The weekly usage for beans and meal remains gigantic," an oilseeds specialist for FIMAT Futures said.
Soybeans also found support on strong commercial stopping of the deliveries posted Monday against the November contract.
Soybeans closed one to 12-1/4 cents per bushel higher, with November up 12-1/4 at $7.11-1/4 a bushel. January was 6-1/2 cents higher at $7.03-1/4.

Term Commodities, the marketing arm of Louis Dreyfus Corp, stopped 4.015 million bushels of the 4.110 million posted Monday for delivery on the November, according to the CBOT. The ADM Investor Services house account posted the 4.110 million for delivery, CBOT records showed.
Traders also cited commercial buying as adding to the gains with Cargill Inc a purchaser of 3.0 million bushels of Januaary. LIT America bought four million January, they said.
Short covering amid thin volume exacerbated the gains in the spot November contract which is slated to expire Tuesday at 1201 CST.
"There could be some fireworks when it goes off, the open interest is still pretty high," a trader said.
Traders said the soybean rally was trimmed by overall good crop weather in key South American soybean growing areas and rapid seeding of the crop in Brazil.

Consultant Safras e Mercado Monday said Brazilian soybean plantings were 43 percent complete by November 14 against 34 percent on the same date a year ago and ahead of the five year average of 36 percent.
Soybean gains also were trimmed by technical selling just under minor resistance in the January which was said near $7.06 a bushel. The session high for January was $7.04-1/2.
First major resistance was said by technicians at $7.01-1/2 a bushel and buy stops were triggered when broad-based buying pushed through that level. Second resistance was at $7.11-1/2.
Soybean futures volume was estimated at 52,000 contracts, down from 59,985 Friday, according to the CBOT.
In soybean options, Lind Waldock bought 1,000 March $7.00 puts and sold 1,000 January $6.75 puts at 19-3/4 to 20-1/4 cents, traders said.
Soybean options volume was estimated at 18,000 contracts, down from 19,340 Friday.
